text:
tanvi: hi all — escalating a customer issue hitting streaming partial outputs + reconnects on their private deployment (VPC + corp proxy). customer sees truncated SSE messages then a reconnect; sometimes the client resends and they get double billed. thread to collect repro, root cause, and next actions

antonia: customer details — AcmeCorp, private deployment in eu-west-1, dedicated nodes. they run an internal corporate proxy (IronProxy) in front of our ingress. symptoms: about 0.3–1% of streaming requests produce 1–2 truncated SSE events (cut mid-line), client immediately reconnects and resumes, sometimes duplicates last chunk. They reported higher rate when payloads > 8KB.

mike: thanks. preliminary guesses: (1) proxy buffering / chunk coalescing or trimming, (2) MTU/MSS blackholing on path between probe->customer proxy->onprem, (3) keepalive/idle timeout on proxy cutting the TCP stream mid-event.

tanvi: I grabbed traces from the customer and our ingress. here's a small SSE fragment they attached (weirdly cut):

```
data: {"seq": 452, "text": "This is a long response that gets cut in the middle of a wor"
```

then the client logs show EPIPE and reconnect immediately.

seb-eng: can you paste the raw tcpdump fragments? curious if the FIN/RST or just an abrupt drop.

antonia: pasted from their support bundle (redacted):
```
18:20:12.345678 IP proxy > backend: Flags [P.], seq 12345:20123, ack 87654, win 65535, length 7778
18:20:12.487123 IP backend > proxy: Flags [.], ack 20123, win 64240, length 0
18:20:12.487456 IP proxy > client: Flags [P.], seq 5634:9188, ack 33445, len 3554  # last TCP packet smaller than application chunk
```

no FIN/RST in that window. looks like the proxy forwarded a smaller packet boundary.

mike: that lines up with PMTU/MSS issues. If a middlebox reduces MTU or strips TCP options, the large writes get split into different packets and some proxies try to coalesce/flush mid-chunk. If the proxy enforces an idle timeout for streaming, it might flush partial buffers and then close.

infra-bot: deployment-check: customer uses dedicated nodes on our private plane; their VPC egress MTU is 9001 (jumbo frames) but their corp proxy is on-prem with default 1500 MTU. Path MTU mismatch detected? run `tracepath` from a node.

tanvi: we asked the customer to run tracepath and also to capture `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing` and to check the proxy config. they returned: tracepath shows pmtu drop at their firewall, and tcp_mtu_probing=0.

seb-eng: repro steps I want to try (dev machine + local proxy):
1) run a simple SSE server that periodically flushes ~10KB `data:` events
2) put nginx proxy with `proxy_buffering on` vs `off` and `proxy_buffer_size 4k`
3) set upstream MTU artificially lower and/or set `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=0` on proxy host
4) observe truncated data + client reconnect pattern

here's a minimal SSE server (node):
```
const http = require('http')
http.createServer((req, res) => {
  res.writeHead(200, {'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache'})
  setInterval(() => {
    const big = 'x'.repeat(10000)
    res.write(`data: ${JSON.stringify({text: big})}\\n\\n`)
  }, 500)
}).listen(3000)
```

use `curl --no-buffer` to observe raw stream.

mike: nginx tips we've seen: set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off; chunked_transfer_encoding on; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection '';` Also ensure `sendfile off; tcp_nopush off;` — some combos help avoid kernel coalescing.

antonia: the customer is running a corporate appliance that doesn't expose nginx config. they were willing to try kernel tweak: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` and reduce their egress MSS via iptables: `iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu`. They applied both and saw immediate reduction in truncated events to ~0.01%.

seb-eng: great signal. still need to rule out application-level buffering. can we add a short sequence-id in every event and have the client dedupe on resume? if they include an `id:` field in SSE, the client can avoid reapplying the last event on reconnect. also we should recommend an `Idempotency-Key` header for the client to avoid duplicate billing if the SDK resends the request.

mike: on our side: add a guard in the billing pipeline to dedupe events within a short window if the same idempotency key is seen for the same customer and route. that's a larger change but should be tracked. For now recommend customers pass `x-redwood-idempotency-key` when calling streaming endpoints, and we will document it.

tanvi: action items:
- mike: open billing dedupe ticket (severity: P2) and spec header behavior. (assigned)
- seb-eng: reproduce locally with nginx and add test to eng-runtime repro-suite (assigned)
- antonia: confirm with customer that kernel + MSS clamp reduced truncation (waiting)
- eng-runtime: consider exposing `streaming.keepalive_timeout` config for private deployments so we can tune proxy-friendly heartbeats per customer

mike: one more note on auth/token rotation: customer had short-lived tokens and a rotation event coincided with an SSE reconnect. when token rotates mid-stream, the client tries to reopen with a new token and our gateway accepted it as a brand-new request. recommend SDKs support seamless token refresh with automatic resume semantics and idempotency header so retries don't double-bill.

antonia: customer confirmed improved behavior after MSS clamp + tcp_mtu_probing=1. they still want us to ship docs for private deploys: checklist for corp proxies (buffering flags, keepalive, MSS clamp) and recommended headers for duplication safety.

tanvi: I'll draft the runbook in support KB and attach the repro code. thanks everyone :pray: 

deploy-bot: deployment note: created support/runbooks/1935072000-sse-windowing-proxy-pathology-draft (internal).
